tools.name: Maths and formulas
tools.summary: Shows formulas and equations in lessons, questions and your answers.

tools.name: Graphs and diagrams
tools.summary: Draws graphs straight from the equations and shows labelled diagrams.

tools.name: Interactive figures
tools.summary: Sliders, small simulations and practice drills inside a lesson. Each runs sealed off from the internet and your files.
tools.for: Any course where trying things helps

tools.name: Lesson sounds
tools.summary: Plays words, tones and notes in lessons, using free recordings from Wikimedia Commons or your computer's own voices.
tools.for: Languages, music and other courses where hearing matters

tools.name: Geometry and graphing
tools.summary: Lets lessons have shapes, points and graphs you can drag and change.
tools.hint:
JSXGraph 1.10 as the global JXG. Make a
, then const b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard("box", {boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false}); and b.create("point", [1, 2]), b.create("slider", [[-4, 4], [0, 4], [0, 1, 3]]), b.create("functiongraph", [x => x * x]), b.create("line", [p, q]), b.create("circle", [p, 2]). So it reads in dark themes, read the theme colours first (const css = v => getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(v).trim()) and before initBoard set JXG.Options.text.strokeColor, JXG.Options.axis.ticks.label.strokeColor and JXG.Options.slider.label.strokeColor to css("--text"), JXG.Options.axis.strokeColor to css("--muted") and JXG.Options.axis.ticks.strokeColor to css("--line"); give each element a strokeColor from css("--chart-1") to css("--chart-6").

tools.name: Sheet music
tools.summary: Shows notes on a stave, so music lessons can show what they teach.
tools.hint:
abcjs 6.4 as the global ABCJS, for showing notation (it can't play sound in a figure; use an audio block for that). Write the music in ABC notation and call ABCJS.renderAbc("paper", "X:1 M:4/4 L:1/4 K:C C D E F | G2 G2 |", {responsive: "resize"}) on a
.

tools.name: 3D molecules
tools.summary: Shows molecules in 3D that you can turn and zoom.
tools.hint:
3Dmol.js 2.4 as the global $3Dmol. Make a
, then const v = $3Dmol.createViewer("mol", {backgroundColor: "white"}); v.addModel(xyzText, "xyz"); v.setStyle({}, {stick: {}, sphere: {scale: 0.25}}); v.zoomTo(); v.render(). Write the atom coordinates inline in XYZ or SDF format (no downloads).

tools.name: World maps
tools.summary: Draws maps of the world and its countries that work offline, for map quizzes and charts.
tools.licence: ISC (map data from Natural Earth, public domain)
tools.hint: D3 7.9 as the global d3, topojson-client as the global topojson, and the world's countries as WORLD_110M (TopoJSON). const land = topojson.feature(WORLD_110M, WORLD_110M.objects.countries); then draw with d3.geoPath(d3.geoEqualEarth().fitSize([600, 320], land)) into an <svg viewBox="0 0 600 320">. Each country feature has properties.name (English).

tools.name: Chess rules
tools.summary: Knows the rules of chess, so a lesson's board can check moves and puzzles.
tools.hint: chess.js 0.13 as the global Chess (move rules only; draw the board yourself with SVG or a grid of buttons). const g = new Chess(fen); g.moves({verbose: true}); g.move({from: "e2", to: "e4"}) returns null for an illegal move; g.fen(), g.in_check(), g.in_checkmate(), g.board().
